clue.text: Height indicators change direction? About time!

indicators.note: the word for altering plus a compass point goes round, or about, the word time

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
taken as written
S, for south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An exasperated pilot welcomes a long-overdue course correction while watching the height gauges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change direction' reads as one phrase about steering, but it splits into a verb and a compass point; 'About' then wraps them round the period.
explanation.definitionFit: Altimeters are the instruments in an aircraft that show how high it is flying.

clue.text: Ex-pupil with degree returns to pulpit

indicators.note: returns says the old pupil and the degree are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A former pupil with a new degree comes back to preach at the school chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised stand in early Christian churches from which the Gospel was read, a kind of pulpit.

clue.text: Unfashionable purpose, to produce wine

indicators.note: IN means fashionable, so being un-fashionable here means losing the letters for in

parts.note: an intent is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: A dated aim of making wine at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfashionable' removes IN (fashionable) from INTENT, leaving TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a deep red Spanish wine, used historically as sacramental wine.

clue.text: Dubious claims copper delayed. (Add up wrongly)

indicators.note: dubious letters are untrustworthy and so get rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A police officer's suspect claims arrive late, with a note that someone has miscounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' rearranges CLAIMS to MISCAL; 'copper' here is the metal, not the police officer it suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscalculate is to get a sum or estimate wrong.

clue.text: As an example of speech, not to be taken literally

definitions.text: As an example of speech, not to be taken literally

parts.words: As an example of speech, not to be taken literally
parts.note: describes a figure of speech, a word used in a figurative rather than literal sense

explanation.surface: A warning that some spoken remark should not be taken at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative use of a word, such as a metaphor, whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Send on elsewhere to study costume

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
a dress is a costume or outfit

explanation.surface: An instruction to post something on to a place where costume can be studied.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a letter is to change its address and forward it.

clue.text: Record one chapter in a long work

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Logging a single chapter of a lengthy book.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem or other lengthy work.

clue.text: Story about Spaniard that may be forgiven

indicators.note: the word for story goes about, or around, the Spaniard

parts.note: a parable is a moral story
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman, so stands for a Spaniard

explanation.surface: A tale of a Spanish man whose misdeeds can be excused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaniard' is a convention: the Spanish title Don stands for any Spanish gentleman, and 'about' wraps the story round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pardonable is excusable, able to be pardoned.

clue.text: Noted by class shortly before narrative in a cathedral?

annotationWithheld.why: Noted by class shortly before narrative in a cathedral? (10): CL (class shortly) + ERE (before) + STORY (narrative) with def 'in a cathedral?' leaves 'Noted by' with no job; the scan prints the same words and no source gives the intended parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Noted by class shortly before narrative in a cathedral?

clue.text: Fleming heroine in a state of servitude?

definitions.meaning: a woman of Ian Fleming's spy hero, a girl belonging to the agent
a woman held in bondage, a female slave

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a possessive it is the spy hero's girl; as one word it is a female slave or serf.

clue.text: Lines and notes from Rabbie's hillside

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran the railway lines in Britain
A is a musical note
E is another musical note

explanation.surface: Lines and notes written by Robert Burns about a Scottish hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbie is Robert Burns, the Scots poet, so the hillside is in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or slope.

clue.text: Hardening process worried stoic in Sofia

indicators.note: worried letters are shaken about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stoic visitor in Bulgaria's capital is anxious about a hardening process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges STOIC IN SOFIA, all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossification is the process by which tissue turns to bone and hardens.

clue.text: Its contents are rearranged by rotation on sound radio

definitions.text: Its contents are rearranged by rotation
definitions.meaning: a tube toy whose coloured pieces form new patterns when turned
the name of a long-running BBC Radio 4 arts programme

explanation.definitionFit: The toy tube of mirrors and coloured glass shifts its pattern when turned, and the same name was used for a BBC radio arts programme.

clue.text: Through which one may view pageants

definitions.meaning: displays or shows put on for an audience

explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are both eyeglasses and grand public shows.

clue.text: Foreign coin I examine is in order

parts.note: the franc was the coin of France and other countries
to scan is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A traveller studying a foreign coin finds it is in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' means belonging to a religious order, not tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Franciscan friar is a member of the religious order founded by St Francis.

clue.text: Take silk, perhaps, and thus decelerate one's downfall

definitions.text: Take silk, perhaps, and thus decelerate one's downfall

parts.words: Take silk, perhaps, and thus decelerate one's downfall
parts.note: take silk suggests a lawyer becoming a QC, but here it is a silk canopy that slows a falling body

explanation.surface: A barrister becomes a senior counsel and so saves their career from ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister who 'takes silk' becomes a Queen's Counsel; here the silk is the fabric of a canopy.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute, once made of silk, slows a person's fall through the air.

clue.text: Dodging obligations, not being orderly officer?

definitions.meaning: shirking what one ought to do
the orderly officer is the one on duty for the day, so one who is not is jokingly not full of duty

explanation.definitionFit: Someone undutiful fails to do what is expected of them; the second reading jokingly splits the word as lacking duty.

clue.text: Unfitting to have forty winks in it

indicators.note: the short sleep goes in the word it

parts.note: forty winks is a short sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: It is unsuitable to take a short sleep at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of the clue is the container signal, so the short sleep sits inside the little pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or not appropriate.

clue.text: Watercourse built by a Pole in California

indicators.note: the article and the pole go in the state's abbreviation

parts.note: N, north, is one of the Earth's poles

explanation.surface: A Polish worker builds a waterway in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is a magnetic pole, not a Polish worker, and 'in' places the article and pole inside the state's short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway.

clue.text: Liquor producer — in dire distress for all that (?).

indicators.note: the word for nevertheless goes in the rearranged letters
distress suggests the letters are troubled and so scrambled

parts.note: still means nevertheless, for all that

explanation.surface: A whisky maker in terrible trouble carries on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' rearranges DIRE into DIER, and 'in' sets the word for 'nevertheless' inside it; the dash is just a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits such as whisky or gin.

clue.text: Relation, as it turns out of a peripatetic lecturer

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative who turns out to be a wandering academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges RELATION AS IT. Aristotle taught while walking, and his school was called the Peripatetic school.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotelian means relating to Aristotle, whose followers were the Peripatetics.

clue.text: Land contract as held in general

indicators.note: held in says the little word is gripped inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A land agreement in which the terms are generally upheld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' points to the American Civil War commander Robert E Lee, and 'held in' wraps his name round the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract letting land or property for a set period.

clue.text: Do you want to go limp?

definitions.meaning: the old second-person form of will
to droop like a flower without water

explanation.definitionFit: Wilt is the archaic thou-form of will, and also means to droop.

clue.text: How this old composer travelled

parts.note: an old English composer's name read as a travel phrase, going by road, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A question about the journeys of a Tudor composer.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Tudor composer; BY RD reads as 'by road'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was an English composer of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Hank of hair that may have a keeper on 18

definitions.meaning: a tress or curl of hair

definitions.text: that may have a keeper on 18
definitions.meaning: a gated section of a waterway, the answer at 18, run by a keeper

explanation.definitionFit: A lock is both a tress of hair and a gated section of a canal that a lock-keeper operates.

clue.text: A fine fellow initially, with capacity for being courteous

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: capacity means ability

explanation.surface: A good man who has the knack of being polite.
explanation.definitionFit: Affability is friendliness and politeness in manner.

clue.text: Bank deposit made by Chopin's girl"

definitions.meaning: material washed up on a riverbank or shore
George ..., the novelist who was Chopin's lover

explanation.definitionFit: Sand is grainy material left on a shore, and the pen name of the writer George Sand, Chopin's companion.

clue.text: Took turns literally to find Dante

parts.note: read literally, the instruction to alter the letters of a word produces Dante

explanation.surface: Literary scholars taking turns to track down the Italian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ALTER NATED, the answer tells you to alter (rearrange) NATED, which gives DANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have alternated is to have done something in turn, one after another.
